ann_87.original: Combined day-and-evening bill gate. The evening charge enters this part twice: through node 103, whose own output lowers the score, and through the chain 103 -> 5908 -> 10233 into gate 9165, where it is added to the day charge; gate 9165 opens when the two charges together are high, and node 14599, which grows with the number of customer service calls, pushes it shut. Prediction: the evening charge raises predicted risk when the day charge is high and slightly lowers it when the day charge is low. Self-probe (typical customer otherwise): with a $20 day charge, raising the evening charge from $10 to $24 moves the whole-model risk from 1.0% to 0.6% and this part's contribution from -0.09 to -2.31 logits; with a $45 day charge the same change moves the risk from 9.4% to 80.5% and the contribution from -0.09 to 1.91 logits. Brake (self-probe): for a customer with a $45 day and $24 evening charge, going from 1 to 5 service calls lowers gate 9165 from 1.56 to 0.42 and this part's contribution from 1.91 to -1.17 logits; in the whole model this customer's risk falls from 80.5% to 59.1%, so for a high-bill customer extra service calls lower the predicted risk. Gate 9165 is open for 1027 of the 4000 training customers; their churn rate is 27.0% against 9.7% for the rest. Switching the part off changes training AUC from 0.914 to 0.901.
ann_87.proposed: This part raises the predicted chance that a customer leaves in an uneven way when the daytime and evening charges are both high, and more calls to customer service push it back down.

Customers with 8 or more calls number 3; the part acts on a share of 100% of them, and their churn rate is 100%. This regime is fitted to 3 rows. On them the part adds 0.44 logits on average, small beside the 10.85 logits added by the whole customer-service group; switching the part off moves training AUC from 0.9144 to 0.9144. ann_90.original: Adds risk that grows in a straight line with each customer service call from the third call on. ann_92.original: High day charge without voicemail messages: node 2149 adds the day charge directly and through a second hinge (14177) that steepens it at high day charges, and each voicemail message pushes it shut. ann_93.original: Holding an international plan raises predicted risk. Node 15558 is open for 380 of the 380 plan holders (a share of 100%), and the count of customers without the plan who have it open is 0. Because its input is a yes/no indicator, its output is a constant for plan holders: it adds 2.82 logits on average. ann_93.proposed: Having an international plan raises the predicted chance that a customer leaves by a fixed amount: for a typical customer, from about 1% to about 17%.

ann_94.original: Units on single-state indicators. Unit 3741 (Rhode Island) is open on every training row (it is open on a share of 100% of rows), so it acts as a linear Rhode Island term; the units for Mississippi (7655, 27279), New Jersey, Utah, New Hampshire and Texas have small output weights. ann_96.original: The four service-call parts add their outputs to the score. For a typical customer they contribute nothing up to 2 calls and then raise the score steeply with each call. ann_98.original: The churn score is the output bias plus the sum of the child parts (customer_service_terms, charge_terms, international_plan, state_units, direct_linear), and the predicted risk is the sigmoid of the score. Because the parts enter the score as a sum, parts that share no inputs add on the logit scale. Self-probe (typical customer): the score is -4.37 with no international plan and 1 call, -2.21 with 4 calls, -1.55 with the plan, and 0.61 with both, the two changes adding; the risk goes from 1.2% to 9.9%, 17.5% and 64.8%. ann_98.proposed: The model adds up five parts to get the predicted chance that a customer leaves: the bill charges, the calls to customer service, fixed amounts per input, the international plan and a few single-state shifts. For a typical customer, who starts at about 1%, a daytime charge of 46.09 US dollars raises it to about 38%, an international plan to about 17% and 4 calls to customer service to about 10% (the charge and the calls each in an uneven way).
